subject: TrueCap #4 — the $850/mo mistake hiding in your insurance line
preheader: Sun Belt insurance up 28% YoY · 3 markets where premiums make or break · CLE, IND, SAC deals

marketSnapshot.headline: Insurance is the new property tax — the silent margin killer
marketSnapshot.body: Property insurance is the biggest line-item change in rental underwriting since rate spike. Sun Belt premiums up 28% YoY in 2025 (FL +42%, LA +35%, TX coastal +29%), Northeast up 8-12%, Midwest flat-to-up-5%. The biggest underwriting mistake I see: investors using the seller's last-year insurance number. Always quote fresh — the gap between 'what they paid' and 'what you'll pay' is often $80-150/mo on a single-family, $200-400/mo on a 2-4 unit.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: 5.9% cap · house hack pencils at 5% down
dealSpotter.body: $485k for a 2/1 + ADU. Owner-occupant FHA gets you in at ~$24k down. ADU rents $1,650; you live in the main house. True out-of-pocket ~$1,100/mo for housing in a market where comparable 2/1 rents go for $2,200. Net: you're paying half-rent to build $9-12k/yr of principal. CA insurance is the wildcard — Tahoe Park is far enough from fire zone that premiums are still in the $1,400-1,800/yr band, not the $4,000+ you'd see closer to fire-zone neighborhoods.

$95k purchase, $1,250 rent. Taxes $1,650, insurance $820/yr (Midwest pricing — under $70/mo). The same property in Tampa would carry $400-450/mo of insurance, completely changing the deal economics. Cleveland's not where you make appreciation money, but it IS where cash flow math is least disrupted by 2024-2026 insurance shocks.

$172k for a renovated 3/2 at $1,675 rent. Neighborhood is in active gentrification (3-year price growth 22%), so this is one of the rare deals where decent cash flow AND appreciation tailwind coexist. Insurance ~$900/yr. Walk the neighborhood at night before pulling the trigger — gentrifying = uneven blocks.

blogFeature.title: Property management yes or no — the actual math
blogFeature.excerpt: 8-10% of rent + lease-up fees + maintenance markup — the all-in cost of property management is usually 13-18% of gross rent, not the 8-10% headline. The honest math on when self-management beats PM and vice-versa.

qa.question: I underwrote a Tampa deal at 8.2% cap, but the insurance quote came back $7,200/yr instead of the $3,800 I assumed. Now it's 6.1%. Do I walk?
qa.answer: Probably. The bigger issue isn't this specific deal — it's that insurance is going to keep moving against you in coastal FL for at least 2-3 more years. Even if you accept the 6.1% today, your year-3 cap rate may be 5.4% as insurance renews up another 20-30%. Run a sensitivity: at insurance +50% from today's quote, does this deal still pencil? If no, the right move is either (a) walk, (b) negotiate price down 10-12% to absorb the future premium hikes, or (c) skip the Sun Belt entirely until insurance markets normalize. Plenty of investors are quietly rotating out of FL/LA to MN/OH/IN for this exact reason.
